text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Foreign Minister Levy: Abolish "kitchen cabinet"; Sharon conditions acceptance of Treasury portfolio on joining inner forum.
- Treasury decides not to issue dollar-linked bonds in July, apparently fearing another shekel devaluation.
- Prime minister's economic adviser says five percent shekel devaluation sufficient.
- Efforts under way to arrange meeting between Levy and Prime Minister Netanyahu.
- Israeli-Palestinian security coordination committee convened, under U.S. auspicies, for first time in many weeks.
- Communications minister might announce today start of competition in international dialling.
- Opening of competition in international calls from Israel could be postponed for several weeks.
- Prime minister's economic adviser says the economy will emerge soon from slowdown.
- Agreement reached on international dialling charges.
- Forex market calms down, traders believe dollar close to stabilising and could fall soon.
- Bezeq faces anti-trust probe of international prices.
